vocabulary.meaning_en: a formal meeting where an employer asks questions to a person who wants a job
vocabulary.note_ar: interviewer = من يُجري المقابلة، interviewee = من تُجرى معه
vocabulary.example: I have a job interview tomorrow at ten.
vocabulary.note_en: interviewer = the person who asks the questions; interviewee = the person who answers them.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person who asks the questions in an interview
vocabulary.example: The interviewer asked about my last job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who is trying to get a job
vocabulary.example: There are five candidates for the position.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a short document (1-2 pages) about your skills and experience
vocabulary.note_ar: مصطلح أمريكي ويُنطق /ˈrezəmeɪ/، ولا تخلطه مع الفعل resume /rɪˈzjuːm/ = يستأنف
vocabulary.example: Please send your résumé by email.
vocabulary.note_en: An American word, pronounced /ˈrezəmeɪ/. Don't confuse it with the verb "resume" /rɪˈzjuːm/ = to start again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a full document about your education and work history
vocabulary.note_ar: اختصار curriculum vitae اللاتينية = مسيرة الحياة
vocabulary.example: My CV is four pages long.
vocabulary.note_en: Short for the Latin "curriculum vitae" = the course of your life.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a letter you send with your CV to explain why you want the job
vocabulary.example: In my cover letter, I explained why I love marketing.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a formal request for a job, often a form
vocabulary.example: Fill in the application and send it before Monday.
vocabulary.note_en: From the verb "apply".

vocabulary.meaning_en: a job that is free and waiting for someone
vocabulary.example: The company has a vacancy for a driver.
vocabulary.note_en: vacant = empty, not taken.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a job or role in a company
vocabulary.example: She applied for the position of sales manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to formally ask for a job
vocabulary.note_ar: يأتي معه حرف الجر for: apply for a job
vocabulary.example: I'm going to apply for that job.
vocabulary.note_en: Used with "for": apply for a job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to get ready for something
vocabulary.example: Prepare answers to common questions.
vocabulary.note_en: prepare for an interview

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell people who you are
vocabulary.example: Can you introduce yourself, please?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to talk about something with someone
vocabulary.note_ar: يأتي بعده الموضوع مباشرة بدون حرف جر: discuss the salary وليس discuss about
vocabulary.example: We discussed the salary at the end of the interview.
vocabulary.note_en: The topic comes directly after it with no preposition: "discuss the salary", not "discuss about".

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give someone a job
vocabulary.example: Why should we hire you?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say no to someone or something
vocabulary.example: They rejected my application, but I'll try again.
vocabulary.note_en: rejection = the act of saying no.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the feeling that you can do things well
vocabulary.example: She answered every question with confidence.
vocabulary.note_en: The adjective is "confident" = sure of yourself.

vocabulary.meaning_en: worried and a little afraid
vocabulary.example: I always feel nervous before an interview.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an ability you learn and practise
vocabulary.example: Communication is an important skill.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a good quality or ability that you have
vocabulary.example: My main strength is teamwork.
vocabulary.note_en: From "strong".

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you are not good at
vocabulary.example: My weakness is speaking in public, but I'm improving.
vocabulary.note_en: From "weak".

vocabulary.meaning_en: knowledge you get from doing a job
vocabulary.note_ar: بمعنى الخبرة العامة غير معدودة: work experience
vocabulary.example: Do you have any experience in sales?
vocabulary.note_en: Meaning general knowledge from work, it is uncountable: work experience.

vocabulary.meaning_en: right for a certain job or purpose
vocabulary.example: I believe I'm suitable for this job.
vocabulary.note_en: suitability = how right someone or something is for a purpose.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having the official training or certificates for a job
vocabulary.example: She is a qualified nurse.
vocabulary.note_en: qualification = a certificate or skill that makes you suitable for a job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: ready
vocabulary.example: I always stay prepared for meetings.

vocabulary.meaning_en: showing the skill and behaviour expected at work
vocabulary.example: He gave a very professional answer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: getting the result you wanted
vocabulary.example: My CV shows successful projects.
vocabulary.note_en: The opposite is "unsuccessful" = did not succeed.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not getting the result you wanted
vocabulary.example: An unsuccessful interview is good practice for the next one.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a period of practical training at a company for students or graduates
vocabulary.example: I did a three-month internship at a bank.
vocabulary.note_en: intern = the trainee.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to finish your studies at a university or school
vocabulary.example: I graduated with a degree in business.
vocabulary.note_en: As a noun, a graduate is a person who has finished university.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a qualification from a university
vocabulary.example: He has a degree in engineering.
vocabulary.note_en: "Degree" also means a unit of temperature.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not long ago
vocabulary.example: I recently moved to a new city.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a choice you make after thinking
vocabulary.example: We will tell you our final decision next week.
vocabulary.note_en: From the verb "decide".

vocabulary.meaning_en: to look for and bring new people to work in a company
vocabulary.example: The company is recruiting five new engineers.
vocabulary.note_en: recruitment = the process of finding and attracting new staff.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to have someone working for you and pay them
vocabulary.example: The factory employs 200 workers.
vocabulary.note_en: employee = worker; employer = the person or company that gives the job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the ability to make new ideas
vocabulary.example: This job needs energy and creativity.
vocabulary.note_en: creative = full of new ideas.

fine_lines.title: recruit vs hire vs employ
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الثلاثة تصف رحلة التوظيف من البداية للنهاية. recruit هو البحث عن الكفاءات وجذبها لتتقدّم للوظيفة. hire هو لحظة الاختيار وقبول الموظف رسمياً. employ هو الحالة المستمرة: الشخص يعمل عندك ويقبض راتبه بانتظام.

examples.sentence: We are recruiting new sales staff this month.
They hired her after one interview.

fine_lines.explanation_en: All three describe the hiring journey from start to finish. "Recruit" means looking for good people and attracting them to apply. "Hire" is the moment you choose someone and officially accept them. "Employ" is the ongoing situation: the person works for you and gets paid regularly.

fine_lines.title: résumé vs CV
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان عن تاريخك المهني. résumé مصطلح أمريكي لوثيقة قصيرة (صفحة أو صفحتان) مفصّلة على مقاس وظيفة محددة، فيها فقط ما يخدم هذه الوظيفة. CV هو المصطلح الشائع في بريطانيا وبقية العالم وفي المجال الأكاديمي والطبي، وهو سجل كامل ومفصّل لكل دراستك وأبحاثك وأعمالك وقد يطول لعدة صفحات.

examples.sentence: Keep your résumé to one page.
Her CV lists all her research papers.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both are about your work history. "Résumé" is the American word for a short document (one or two pages) made for one specific job, with only the information that helps for that job. "CV" is the common word in Britain and the rest of the world, and in academic and medical fields; it is a full, detailed record of all your studies, research and work, and it can be several pages long.

fine_lines.title: résumé vs resume
fine_lines.explanation_ar: تُكتبان بحروف متشابهة لكن المعنى والنطق مختلفان. résumé اسم = سيرة ذاتية ويُنطق «ريزيوميه». resume فعل = يستأنف (يكمل بعد توقف) ويُنطق «ريزيوم».

examples.sentence: I updated my résumé last night.
The meeting will resume after lunch.

fine_lines.explanation_en: They are spelled almost the same, but the meaning and pronunciation are different. "Résumé" is a noun = a document about your work history, pronounced "REZ-yoo-may". "Resume" is a verb = to continue after a stop, pronounced "ri-ZYOOM".

fine_lines.title: Past simple vs present perfect in interviews
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الماضي البسيط لحدث انتهى في وقت محدد (سنة، الصيف الماضي). المضارع التام لعرض خبرتك وإنجازاتك العامة التي تفيدك الآن، بدون ذكر وقت محدد.

examples.sentence: I have managed many marketing campaigns.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Use the past simple for an event that finished at a specific time (a year, last summer). Use the present perfect to show your general experience and achievements that help you now, without saying when.

expressions.meaning_ar: يبخس نفسه حقها / يقلّل من قيمة مهاراته
expressions.example: You have five years of experience, so don't sell yourself short.
expressions.meaning_en: to show yourself as less skilled or valuable than you really are

expressions.example: He applied for three jobs this week.
expressions.meaning_en: to ask officially to be given a job

expressions.meaning_ar: لماذا يجب أن نوظّفك؟ (سؤال شائع في المقابلات)
expressions.example: Prepare a strong answer to "Why should we hire you?"
expressions.meaning_en: a common interview question asking why you are the best person for the job

expressions.example: I'm organized and I work well in a team.
expressions.meaning_en: to work successfully with other people

expressions.example: Many people get nervous when they speak in public.
expressions.meaning_en: to talk in front of an audience

expressions.example: The manager will make the final decision on Friday.
expressions.meaning_en: the last decision that settles something

grammar.title: Past simple: finished events at a specific time
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم الماضي البسيط لحدث انتهى في وقت محدد ومغلق في الماضي، خاصة مع كلمات مثل in 2023, last summer, yesterday.
examples: I finished my internship last summer.
Did you prepare the report this morning?
grammar.explanation_en: Use the past simple for an event that finished at a specific, closed time in the past, especially with words like "in 2023", "last summer", "yesterday".

grammar.title: Present perfect: experience that matters now
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم have/has + التصريف الثالث لعرض خبراتنا وإنجازاتنا المتراكمة التي تفيد الآن، بدون ذكر وقت محدد. سؤال Have you ever...? يسأل عن خبرتك العامة.
examples: She has prepared many financial reports.
Have you ever built a website?
grammar.explanation_en: Use have/has + past participle to show your experience and achievements that matter now, without saying exactly when. The question "Have you ever...?" asks about your general experience.

questions.question: A person who is trying to get a job is a:
questions.explanation_en: A candidate is a person who applies for a job.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: discuss يأتي بعده الموضوع مباشرة بدون حرف جر.
questions.explanation_en: The topic comes directly after "discuss", with no preposition.

questions.question: I ___ from university in 2022.
questions.explanation_ar: وقت محدد في الماضي (2022) فنستخدم الماضي البسيط.
questions.explanation_en: 2022 is a specific time in the past, so we use the past simple.

questions.question: To show your general experience, you say: "I ___ many marketing campaigns."
questions.explanation_ar: المضارع التام لعرض الخبرة العامة بدون وقت محدد.
questions.explanation_en: The present perfect shows general experience without a specific time.

questions.question: The company ___ 300 people. (they work there now and get paid)
questions.explanation_ar: employ = حالة مستمرة، الناس يعملون عندك.
questions.explanation_en: "Employ" is an ongoing situation: people work for you now.

questions.question: "Don't sell yourself short" means:
choices: Don't make your skills seem less than they are.
questions.explanation_ar: sell yourself short = يبخس نفسه حقها.
questions.explanation_en: "Sell yourself short" = to show yourself as less valuable than you are.

questions.question: Which is a short American document about your skills (1-2 pages)?
questions.explanation_ar: résumé وثيقة أمريكية قصيرة مفصّلة على وظيفة محددة.
questions.explanation_en: A résumé is a short American document made for one specific job.

questions.question: "The meeting will resume at 3" means the meeting will:
questions.explanation_en: As a verb, "resume" means to continue after a stop.

questions.question: A job that is free and waiting for someone is a:
questions.explanation_en: A vacancy is a job that is free and waiting for someone.

questions.question: "I always feel ___ before an interview, so I practise a lot."
questions.explanation_en: Nervous = worried and a little afraid.
